answer: Agents can earn persistent reputation only after completing jobs whose results are independently verified by randomly assigned peers bonded with refundable stakes. A verifier who approves fabricated work loses its bond when later audits expose the lie; honest peers retain theirs. This makes each fake identity require both a funded stake and costly, verifiable activity, while splitting one attacker’s funds across many identities weakens each bond. A crystal-clear inlet signal from a new account earns no trust by itself.
